per_subject_ii_a_annotations_as_replicat.definition: targets=19 subjects; replicates = every individual annotation of every image of that subject (n per subject 190-552)

per_subject_ii_b_image_means_as_replicat.definition: targets=19 subjects; replicates = per-image mean rating (38-111 images per subject)

per_subject_ii_c_image_medians_as_replic.definition: targets=19 subjects; replicates = per-image median rating

per_subject_iii_within_subject.definition: ICC(1) computed separately within each subject with targets = that subject's images

paper_ranges.note: paper ranges are across 5 regions + global pool (25 ratings/image); here 1 region, <=5 ratings/image

c_variance.note: No annotator IDs: the within-image residual mixes rater leniency (main effect), rater x image interaction and pure error; it cannot be split. Image(subject) variance = true between-image change in perceived tone (lighting/pose) as seen through the crowd.

d_spread.note: golden_like_random_draws: 2000 draws of one random image per subject (subjects within the oracle window), interval = 2.5/97.5 percentiles over draws (Monte Carlo spread of the design, not a sampling CI).

subject_level_consensus_vs_oracle.definition: for each of 19 subjects, take k random raters per image (all images of the subject; 4-rating images contribute min(k,4)); consensus = median of all selected ratings (pooled) or median of image medians; compare with oracle. Intervals = Monte Carlo 2.5/97.5 over 500 rater draws (not a sampling CI; n=19 subjects).

e_k_raters.note: Only the 1467 images with 5 ratings are used (15 four-rating images dropped; this removes 1 Challenging image -> Challenging n=18). vs5 compares the k-rater median with the 5-rater median that CONTAINS those k raters (inflated by overlap); heldout compares with the median of the other 5-k raters (disjoint). Even-k medians can be x.5: "raw" uses np.median; heldout for k=2 and k=3 are the same comparisons (2 vs other 3);  "randtie" = expected value when the tie is broken at random (mean of lower/upper median).

meta.n: 19 subjects / 1482 images (1467x5 + 15x4 ratings) / 7395 annotations, one region (labelled Ghana)
meta.bands: light: oracle 1-3 (7 subj); mid: 4-7 (7 subj); dark: 8-10 (5 subj)
